newsitem.title: UK: NatWest off as Dresdner joins downgrade pack.
newsitem.headline: NatWest off as Dresdner joins downgrade pack.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc eased on Thursday as the latest of a group of brokers cut its profit estimates following a briefing from the bank, dealers said.
The stock dipped as low as 776p before paring losses as the market rose to trade at 783-1/2p, 2-1/2p lower, midmorning.

Dresdner Kleinwort Benson cut its 1997 pre-tax figure to 1,759 million stg from 1,906 million and by ten million to 1,954 million for next year based on costs creeping higher and slowing income, dealers said.
Dresdner Kleinwort analysts declined to comment.

NatWest shares closed 18p lower at 786p on Wednesday after Salomon cut earnings estimates. Analyst John Leonard trimmed by 70 million stg for this year to 1,825 million stg and to 2,055 million from 2,125 million for 1998.
In 1996 the company made pre-tax profits of 1,122 million stg.

On Tuesday, SocGen also lowered its NatWest earnings estimates, bringing its top-end figures in line with the market consensus, yet the outlook for the bank's shares is probably more tied up with recent talk of possible bids and mergers in the bank sector, dealers said.

NatWest has been seen as under pressure to do a deal, possibly with a domestic rival such as Abbey National Plc, to improve shareholder returns and tackle the recent underperformance of its shares, they said.
Last week ABN AMRO Hoare Govett cut its estimates by 130 million stg to 1,820 million stg for 1997 and by 100 million to 2.3 billion for next year after a meeting with the bank.
Hoare analysts said they based the downgrade on higher than expected bad debts and losses(of about 77 million)incurred by NatWest Markets through options trading.
SBC Warburg and UBS are due to see NatWest next week.
NatWest reports half-year results on August 5.
